page: Microsoft Azure M32bds_v3 is a memory-optimized virtual machine provisioned on Microsoft Hyper-V. It is powered by a dedicated 4.0 GHz Intel Xeon 8473C processor featuring 16 physical cores and 32 vCPUs via hyperthreading. The instance includes 256.0 GB of memory, providing an 8.0 GB RAM-to-vCPU ratio. Local storage consists of a 429 GB SSD, and no GPUs are present. The underlying x86_64 architecture incorporates instruction extensions including AVX-512, AMX (Tile and INT8), and cryptographic primitives like AES and SHA-NI.

Benchmark results show solid general-purpose and single-core capabilities, registering a Geekbench single-core score of 2197.0 and a multi-core score of 18223.0, both placing in the top quartile. Throughput workloads perform well, highlighted by 52.78 GB/sec in static web serving tests, 32.77 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression, and 213.19 GB/sec in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Standard stress-ng and PassMark tests report mid-tier results, such as a multi-core stress-ng score of 33775.96 and a PassMark CPU score of 47552.95.

Data structure and caching operations operate comfortably in the mid-range, as reflected by Redis SET throughput measuring 44.19 million operations per second and PassMark database operations at 17058.22. Without dedicated hardware accelerators, CPU-bound LLM inference varies widely: smaller models yield up to 312.22 tokens/sec during generation, whereas large 70B parameter models fall into the lower quartile at 2.74 tokens/sec.

The hardware profile delivers balanced resource density for workloads demanding high memory capacity per core without necessitating GPU compute. M32bds_v3 is suited for enterprise relational databases, large in-memory caches, data analytics pipelines, and memory-intensive web serving environments.
description: Microsoft Azure M32bds_v3 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon 8473C processor delivering 32 dedicated vCPUs (16 physical cores) at 4.0 GHz. Configured with 256.0 GB of system memory, an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio, and a local 429 GB SSD, this instance addresses workloads that exceed typical general-purpose memory requirements. Benchmark evaluations indicate top-tier results in single-threaded gzip compression (32.77 GB/sec), Geekbench multi-core execution (18223.0), and static web serving throughput (52.78 GB/sec), balanced by median performance in PassMark CPU tests and Redis SET operations (44.19 million ops/sec). Lacking a dedicated accelerator, large model AI inference represents an operational tradeoff. The instance offers appropriate cost efficiency for memory-heavy computing, enterprise relational database systems, in-memory caching platforms, and data warehousing tasks.
